newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Japan urges Australia link in Asian projects.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Japan urges Australia link in Asian projects.

text.p: Japanese Deputy Foreign Minister Kazuo Ogura has called on Australian business to link with Japanese interests to bid for US$1.5 trillion of energy-related infrastructure projects in Asia through the use of billions of dollars a year worth of Japan's Official Development Assistance.

Kazuo Ogura told a session at the inaugural meeting of Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation region energy ministers here on Thursday that despite growing unpopularity of Japan's big ODA programme within Japan, the Japanese government wished to use it to help close financial gaps in Asia's infrastructure programme.
"Australian business is able to make use of (ODA) because it's (ODA) for international bidding," Ogura said.
"You could make joint-ventures with Japanese enterprises, for instance," he said.

Ogura's comments strengthen a trend by big Japanese companies to link Japan's ODA funds, worth about $70 billion in the current 1992-1997 plan or $14.7 billion in 1995, to back consortiums formed between Japanese and overseas groups to bid for Asian infrastructure projects.

The Australian arm of Japan's biggest trading house, Mitsui and Co Ltd, recently revealed that it was forming several consortiums with Australian companies to bid for Asian infrastructure projects with the backing of Japanese ODA funds.
ODA is becoming increasingly unpopular in Japan because Japanese business would not necessarily profit from it, Ogura said.
Now 98 percent of Japanese yen credits were untied, Ogura said.
The senior Japanese official said governments could help close gaps in Asia's energy infrastructure funding programme.
The Japanese government for the past two years had been styudying ways risk could be shared between governments, he said.

Ogura released a government-backed study by Nomura Research Institute which stated that the Japanese government should consider furnishing yen credit and other forms of public sector financing for privately-led infrastructure projects.

The Japanese foreign ministry recently began setting objectives for Japan's sixth ODA programme for 1998-year 2002 and is hoping to deflect domestic criticism by stressing quality rather than quantity.
The World Bank has estimated that Asian funding demands for infrastructure development will range between $1.3 trillion and $1.5 trillion between 1995 and year 2004.
